05 / FAQ

Questions.

What is OneOS?

OneOS is a catalog that lists every operating system available for a range of Galaxy phones. It shows which systems each model supports, which builds have been tested, and how the systems differ.

What does “tested” mean?

A build marked as tested has been confirmed working on that specific model. Builds that started only on some tries are marked “Works on some tries”, builds that never started are marked “Does not start”, and builds nobody has tried yet are marked “Untested”. Treat all of them as experimental.

Where you see a green ring around a dot, that build is tested.

What is the difference between an OEM skin, stock Android and a custom ROM?

OEM skins such as ColorOS, OriginOS, HyperOS and Nothing OS are made by phone manufacturers and usually come with extra features and a distinct design.

Stock Android is the clean reference experience, as seen on Pixel phones.

Custom ROMs like LineageOS and Infinity-X are community projects, often focused on privacy, longevity or customization.

Why do some phones have fewer options than others?

Support depends on the hardware. Older and budget models have fewer builds that are compatible with their chipsets, so some of them only offer a handful of systems.

Is it safe to switch?

Switching operating systems can erase your data. Back up your photos, messages, contacts and app data before you start, and prefer tested builds.

Where do the ratings come from?

They are editorial opinions about each system’s general character, on a scale of 1 to 5. They are not benchmarks and do not account for any specific device.

Will switching affect my warranty?

It can. Unlocking the bootloader is the usual first step for custom systems, and on many phones it is permanent or leaves a mark the manufacturer can see. Read your region’s warranty terms before you start.

Can I go back to the original software?

Usually yes, if you saved the stock firmware for your exact model first. That is why it is worth downloading it before you begin. Going back also wipes your data.

Why are there Snapdragon and Exynos versions of the same phone?

Some models ship with different chipsets in different regions. Builds are made for one chipset family, so always match the model number and codename, not just the phone’s name.
